newsitem.title: USA: USDA downplays statements on Canada wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: USDA downplays statements on Canada wheat exports.

text.p: The head of the Agriculture Department's Foreign Agricultural Service downplayed statements he made earlier on Thursday that Canada will try to limit wheat exports to the U.S. this year to no more than 1.5 million tonnes.

"In my comments I reflected on my impressions from our Canadian discussions that the Canadians were not expecting that the 1.4, 1.5 million tonnes of wheat exports would be much exceeded in this marketing year," said FAS administrator August Schumacher.
"If this impression was misunderstood to imply a voluntary limit by the Canadians, this is an incorrect interpretation of our impressions from these discussions," Schumacher said.
Schumacher raised a ruckus among officials in Ottawa earlier in the day when he said, "We understand they (Canada) have told us they would try not to exceed this amount (1.4 to 1.5 million tonnes)."
Schumacher, speaking to a House Agriculture panel, said at the time that officials were trying to clarify these reports.

Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale strongly denied that Canada would be willing to limit its grain exports. "The U.S. allegations are completely, utterly, absolutely unfounded and wrong," he told reporters.

Schumacher told reporters after his remarks to lawmakers that Canadian officials were discussing voluntarily limiting their wheat exports to the United States. He noted that whether to cap exports is a "very difficult" problem for Canadian officials politically, but said, "We hope this is what they do."
Another senior USDA official said of the possibility of Canada capping its exports -- "We would certainly like it if they would ... (but) I am skeptical if they would consider that."

U.S. and Canadian officials are scheduled to begin grain consultations next week in Canada. Schumacher said the United States will be discussing a "number of things" with the Canadians during the talks, but later refused to say if Washington would specifically push for export limits.
